title: Latency hedging exporter and cost-aware endpoint selector for trace writes
creator: Alex Nguyen
description:
Background:
Redwood's current OTLP exporter/router sends spans to a single backend per-tenant based on configured routing policy. During region/back-end degradation or transient spikes, write latencies to the primary backend (Tempo or Jaeger) can cross SLOs and cause long tail latency for request lifecycles that depend on synchronous span delivery.

Goal:
Build a resilient 'latency-hedging' exporter and an interleaved cost-aware endpoint selector that: 1) reduces tail latency for trace writes by speculatively hedging to a secondary backend when primary latency crosses a threshold; 2) enforces per-tenant cost budgets and rate limits so hedging does not explode downstream billing; 3) preserves trace correctness via idempotency keys and deduplication markers so multiple writes from hedged attempts don't create duplicate spans in long-retention stores.

High-level design notes:
- Hedging policy: exporter measures rolling P95/P99 write latency per-backend and tenant. If primary's write latency exceeds configurable threshold (default: 300ms), the exporter sends a hedged write to a secondary backend after a short delay (default: 50ms hedging delay).
- Endpoint selector: combines capability score (supported features, schema version), latency signal, and a cost multiplier derived from tenant billing tier and per-backend egress cost to pick primary and fallback candidates.
- Cost-aware budget: each tenant has a hedging budget (tokens per minute). Hedging consumes tokens proportional to payload size. When budget is exhausted, exporter stops hedging for that tenant and falls back to best-effort single-write path.
- Idempotency and dedupe: exporter attaches deterministic write-id (sha256(span-batch + tenant-id + sequence)) and a hedging-marker header. Backends must accept de-duplication hints; for incompatible backends write a lightweight envelope with write-id so downstream dedupe processors can prune duplicates.
- Backpressure and backoff: exporter observes backend 429/5xx and increases hedging delay, reduces hedging rate, and reports metrics. Hedged writes should honor per-backend concurrency lanes to avoid amplification.

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: per-tenant hedging_attempts, hedging_success_rate, hedging_cost_units_consumed, hedged_duplicate_count, write_latency_primary, write_latency_secondary, hedging_budget_remaining; expose as Prometheus-compatible counters/gauges.
- Dashboards: drive a latency vs cost dashboard that correlates hedging attempts with total egress cost and P99 write latency across tenants. Include drilldown to tenant-level budget burn and top hedged endpoints.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end integration test that simulates primary backend slowdowns and verifies hedged writes reduce P99 write latency by >=40% for targeted tenants without exceeding budget limits.
- Backfill/dedupe test ensures no duplicate spans are created in Tempo/Jaeger long-term storage when hedging is enabled.
- Metric coverage to show hedging attempts, budget consumption, and per-tenant cost delta in staging dashboards.
- A migration/compatibility doc for backends that do not understand write-id/dedupe headers, describing envelope format and downstream deduper requirement.

Progress updates and open tasks:
- 2026-03-02: Spike completed. Implemented prototype exporter that sends hedged write after fixed delay. Prototype simulated on local mock Tempo and reduced P99 48% in the scenario. Link to spike notes: https://confluence.redwood/company/observability/hedging-spike
- 2026-03-04: Design review with infra and platform teams. Feedback: (a) require explicit opt-in per-tier for hedging to prevent uncontrolled cost; (b) prefer token bucket style budget to simplify enforcement; (c) add defensive max-duplicate threshold to avoid noisy spikes. Action: updated design to token-bucket budget and included per-tenant opt-in flag.
- 2026-03-06: Implemented hedging delay and token-bucket enforcement in exporter branch. Unit tests for token consumption and backoff logic added. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821.
- 2026-03-07: Integration test failing intermittently when upstream returns 503 and then accepts hedged write; root cause appears to be dedupe marker ordering. Next: coordinate with backend team on a deterministic write-id canonicalization and idempotency contract.

Design trade-offs and considerations:
- Cost vs latency: aggressive hedging reduces latency but increases egress and storage costs. We mitigate via per-tenant budget and opt-in. Short hedging delay reduces latency wins but creates more duplicate work; choose defaults conservatively and let customers tune.
- Dedupe guarantees: perfect dedupe requires backend support or a downstream dedupe processor. For incompatible backends we will rely on a best-effort envelope with write-id and implement server-side dedupe in writable ingestion path.
- Complexity: adding hedging logic to the exporter increases operational surface area. To minimize risk we will provide a toggled rollout (console feature flag + canary by tenant) and strong observability.

Open questions:
1) Should hedging be allowed for high-volume infra tenants by default or strictly opt-in? (Design review leaned opt-in for customer cost protection.)
2) Is write-id canonicalization acceptable for all backends (UTF-8 normalization + sorted fields)? Backend teams to confirm.
3) Should we add a per-tenant cost-predictor that estimates expected extra bill given current hedging parameters? (Nice-to-have for Console).

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Coordinate with backend ingestion owners to finalize idempotency header semantics and dedupe envelope (assigned to @Samira Lopez).
- Stabilize dedupe ordering in integration test and add randomized fuzz tests for delayed ack scenarios (owner: Priya Kapoor).
- Add Prometheus metric exporters and a draft dashboard for the staging cluster (owner: Observability Infra).
- Prepare console rollout flag and tenant opt-in flow for QA in staging (owner: Product).
